spec: Write a function that checks whether a list of numbers has at least one index i such that the sum of the elements before index i equals the sum of the elements after index i (the element at index i itself is excluded from both sums). Return True if such an index exists and False otherwise, including for an empty list.

Write a function that treats a list of numbers as weights placed at positions 0, 1, 2, and so on, and computes the weighted average position (the sum of index times value, divided by the sum of the values), rounded to the nearest integer using standard Python rounding. Return -1 if the sum of the values is zero.

Write a function that takes a list of numbers and a threshold t, and splits the list into two lists: one containing all elements strictly less than t, and one containing all elements greater than or equal to t, each preserving the original relative order. Return the two lists as a tuple (below, at_or_above).

Write a function that splits a list of numbers into two parts at the position of the first negative number: everything before it, and everything from it onward (inclusive). Return the two parts as a tuple (before, from_first_negative_onward). If there is no negative number, return the whole list as the first part and an empty list as the second.

Write a function that splits a list of integers into two lists based on parity: one containing the even values and one containing the odd values, each preserving the original relative order (this works correctly for negative integers as well). Return the two lists as a tuple (evens, odds).

Write a function that splits a list of numbers into two parts at the position of the first zero: everything before it, and everything from it onward (inclusive). Return the two parts as a tuple (before, from_zero_onward). If there is no zero in the list, return the whole list as the first part and an empty list as the second.

Write a function that splits a list of numbers into consecutive runs where each run contains only numbers of the same sign category: positive, negative, or zero. Return a list of sublists, one per maximal run, in the order they occur. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that splits a list of integers into consecutive runs where each run contains only numbers of the same parity (all even or all odd). Return a list of sublists, one per maximal run, in the order they occur. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that pairs up elements from two lists by matching index, producing a list of tuples (a[i], b[i]), extending the shorter list with a given pad value so the result has as many pairs as the length of the longer list. Return an empty list if both inputs are empty.

Write a function that takes a list of pairs (tuples or lists of exactly two elements) and splits it into two separate lists: one with all the first elements, and one with all the second elements, both preserving order. Return a tuple of the two lists, both empty, if the input list is empty.

Write a function that combines three lists element by index into a list of triples (a[i], b[i], c[i]). If the lists have different lengths, stop at the length of the shortest list. Return an empty list if the shortest input is empty.
Write a function that takes a list and returns a list of (index, value) tuples for every element, in order, starting the index count at 0. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that computes the running maximum of a list of numbers: the i-th element of the result is the maximum of all elements from the start of the list up to and including index i. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that computes the running minimum of a list of numbers: the i-th element of the result is the minimum of all elements from the start of the list up to and including index i. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that computes the running minimum from the right of a list of numbers: the i-th element of the result is the minimum of all elements from index i to the end of the list. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that computes, for each position i in a list of numbers, the difference between the running maximum and running minimum of the elements from the start of the list up to and including index i. Return the resulting list of ranges, which is empty for an empty input.

Write a function that returns the list of indices at which a list of numbers reaches a new strict running maximum (an element strictly greater than every element before it). The first element, if the list is non-empty, always counts as establishing the first running maximum. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that computes an alternating sum over a list of numbers, adding the element at index 0, subtracting the element at index 1, adding the element at index 2, and so on, alternating signs starting with a plus. Return 0 for an empty list.

Write a function that computes an alternating sum over a list of numbers, subtracting the element at index 0, adding the element at index 1, subtracting the element at index 2, and so on, alternating signs starting with a minus. Return 0 for an empty list.

Write a function that computes the absolute differences between each pair of consecutive elements in a list of numbers, then sums those differences with alternating signs, starting with a plus for the first difference, minus for the second, and so on. Return 0 if the list has fewer than two elements.

Write a function that checks whether a list of numbers 'zigzags': every interior element must be either strictly greater than both of its neighbors or strictly less than both of its neighbors, with no two consecutive elements equal anywhere in the list. Lists with fewer than 2 elements are trivially considered to zigzag; a list of exactly 2 distinct elements also zigzags. Return True or False.

Write a function that counts how many times the sign changes between consecutive elements in a list of numbers, treating each number's sign as negative, zero, or positive (so a change to or from zero also counts as a sign change if the categories differ). Return 0 for a list with fewer than 2 elements.

Write a function that rearranges a list of integers so that all even numbers come first, followed by all odd numbers, with each group preserving its original relative order from the input list. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that rearranges a list of integers so that all odd numbers come first, followed by all even numbers, with each group preserving its original relative order from the input list. Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that moves all negative numbers in a list to the front, while preserving the original relative order of the negative elements and of the non-negative elements. Return an empty list for an empty input.
Write a function that counts the number of adjacent pairs in a list of numbers where the second element is strictly greater than the first. Return 0 for a list with fewer than 2 elements.
Write a function that counts the number of adjacent pairs in a list of numbers where the second element is strictly less than the first. Return 0 for a list with fewer than 2 elements.

Write a function that checks whether a list of numbers forms a geometric sequence, meaning the ratio between every pair of consecutive elements is the same constant. The list is assumed to contain no zero values. Lists with 0 or 1 elements are trivially considered geometric. Return True or False.
Write a function that sorts a list of numbers and finds the maximum difference between two consecutive values in that sorted order. Return 0 if the list has fewer than 2 elements.

Write a function that counts local maxima in a list, where an interior element is a local maximum if it is strictly greater than both its neighbors, and an endpoint (first or last element) is a local maximum if it is strictly greater than its single neighbor. A list of exactly one element counts as having one local maximum, and an empty list has zero. Return the count as an integer.

Write a function that takes a list of numbers and a target value, and finds the smallest index i such that the sum of the elements from the start of the list up to and including index i is strictly greater than the target. Return that smallest index, or -1 if the running sum never exceeds the target.

Write a function that computes a running total of a list of numbers, but whenever adding the next element makes the running total negative, the total is reset to 0 at that position instead of being allowed to go negative. Return the list of running totals recorded after each element is processed (and possibly reset), which is empty for an empty input.

Write a function that finds the maximal run of consecutive strictly positive numbers with the greatest number of elements, and returns the sum of that run's elements. If multiple runs tie for the greatest length, use the first one encountered. Return 0 if the list has no positive numbers.

Write a function that merges two lists that are each already sorted in ascending order into a single sorted ascending list, similar to the merge step of merge sort. Assume both input lists are sorted; ties should take from the first list before the second. Return an empty list if both inputs are empty.

Write a function that shifts the elements of a list to the left by n positions, dropping the first n elements and filling the last n positions with a given fill value; the result has the same length as the input. If n is 0 or negative, return a copy of the list unchanged; if n is at least the length of the list, return a list of the fill value repeated to the original length.

Write a function that finds the smallest positive integer (1 or greater) that does not appear in a list of integers. The list may contain negatives, zero, duplicates, or be unordered. Return that smallest missing positive integer.

Write a function that takes a list of unique integers sorted in ascending order and compresses it into a list of [start, end] pairs, one for each maximal run of consecutive integers (each next value equal to the previous plus one). Return an empty list for an empty input.

Write a function that finds the maximum product obtainable by multiplying two distinct-position elements from a list of numbers (the list may contain negative numbers, so the best pair might be the two largest or the two most negative values). Assume the list has at least two elements.
Write a function that finds the minimum absolute difference between any two distinct-position elements of a list of numbers. Assume the list has at least two elements.

Write a function that takes a list of lists and returns the length of the longest common prefix shared by all of them, where a prefix is common if every list has the same value at each of those leading positions. Return 0 if the outer list is empty or if the lists share no common leading value.
